alerts.reason: Buckle's Q3 net sales fell 3.2% (A) even as average price per piece rose 2.8% (D), implying roughly 5.9% fewer pieces sold. If that unit decline persists, a smaller price increase could take sales growth to -5% within two quarters.

Boston Beer's revenue rose just 0.6% as pricing and lower returns offset a 1.9% shipment decline (A, B). Distributors held 5.5 weeks of inventory against a 4–5 week target (C). Cutting orders to reach that target could push quarterly revenue growth to -5% within two quarters.

TreeHouse's net sales decline widened from 1.87% to 2.80% (A). Hurricane Helene disrupted distribution and cost an estimated $5–10 million in volume/mix (B). A full quarter of disruption, if it persisted, could close the remaining 2.20-point gap.

Lincoln Electric attributed lower sales to “softer demand across all segments” in both the three- and nine-month periods (A). Quarterly net sales growth fell from -3.67% to -4.79%, leaving just 0.21 percentage points to cross if demand weakens further in either of the next two quarters.

Amkor's Q3 net sales grew just 2.2% despite 30% consumer and 23% computing growth, as communications and automotive/industrial sales fell (A, B). Elevated customer inventories and weaker demand drove a 17% nine-month automotive/industrial decline (C). Continued order weakness could pull consolidated growth to -5% within two quarters if consumer and computing gains ease.

Mesa's operating revenue swung from 8.0% growth to a 3.4% decline (A). The retirement and sale of several aircraft (D) could constrain flying capacity over the next two quarters, when a further 1.6-point deterioration would reach -5%.

Universal Logistics' consolidated revenue growth slowed from 12.02% to 1.33%. Load volume fell 13.2% while revenue per load excluding fuel rose only 1.8% (B), and fuel surcharges fell $6.3 million (C). Further load losses at that pace could erase the remaining growth and push revenue to a 5% decline within two quarters.
